title: Chronological checkpointing for streaming metering to resolve out-of-order fragments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our streaming ingestion occasionally receives fragments for the same session out of order (retries, network replays, multiplexed clients). Current metering aggregates naively by arrival time which causes double-counting or dropped credits when fragments are replayed or reordered. Goal: implement a chronological checkpointing and anchored-ack scheme so the metering pipeline attributes input/output tokens deterministically and can reconcile replays without manual interventions.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a monotonic fragment_cursor (session_uuid + fragment_seq) persisted as checkpoints and used by the aggregator
Aggregator ignores fragments older-or-equal-to the persisted cursor per session unless fragment_checksum shows previously missing tokens
End-to-end integration test that replays fragments out of order shows identical billed token totals compared to in-order baseline
Backfill reconciliation exposes less than 0.1% discrepancy on last 30 days; remaining discrepancies have automated drift tickets
No visible increase in tail latency for real-time metering path under 99th percentile SLA
technical_notes: Design: add fragment_seq (int64), fragment_checksum (sha256 hex) and capture_time_utc columns to metering_events table; each stream session is anchored by persisted checkpoint row with last_committed_seq and last_committed_checksum

Ingress: attach session_uuid and fragment_seq at ingest layer. Source libraries (JS/Go SDKs) will monotonically increment fragment_seq for client-side retries; server assigns seq when missing but flags as optimistic and requires server-side dedupe

Checkpointing algorithm: when aggregator processes fragment F(session, seq): fetch checkpoint C for session; if seq <= C.last_committed_seq and checksum != C.last_committed_checksum then enqueue for reconciliation job; if seq <= C.last_committed_seq and checksum == C.last_committed_checksum then drop as duplicate; else apply fragment and advance checkpoint atomically

Atomicity: use lightweight compare-and-swap on Postgres row for checkpointing (FOR UPDATE) to guarantee single-writer progress per session window. If performance concerns arise we will evaluate Redis CAS with durable backup to PG
Watermarking: maintain per-shard watermark to GC old sessions and to trigger reconciliation window (default 48h). Watermark advances based on commit progress and time-based heuristics
Reconciliation job: idempotent map-reduce that computes expected tokens per session using fragment checksums and aggregates to billing ledger; emits corrective ledger entries when drift > threshold
Observability: add metrics: checkpoint_advances_total, checkpoint_conflicts_total, reconciliation_jobs_run, reconciliation_corrections_total, fragment_deduped_total
Edge cases: multiplexed clients that interleave sessions must use session_uuid; long-lived sessions (>30 days) will be segmented by segment_id to avoid unbounded seq growth

Trade-offs: strictly enforcing client-side monotonic seq reduces server complexity but requires SDK upgrades; server-assigned seq supports compatibility but increases dedupe complexity and may require more reconciliation runs
migration_plan: 1) DB migration: add fragment_seq, fragment_checksum, capture_time_utc, checkpoint table. Deploy schema in read-only mode and verify ingestion succeeds
2) SDK rollouts: release JS/Go SDKs to start emitting fragment_seq; support legacy clients by assigning server-side seq with server-flagged optimistic_seq
3) Backfill: run signer job that computes fragment_checksum for historical rows and seeds checkpoint table using heuristics (last seen seq per session)
4) Enable aggregator to consult checkpoints in a canary region for 24 hours, compare totals against baseline aggregator, and monitor checkpoint_conflicts_total
5) Flip default to strict checkpointing and enable reconciliation job for historical discrepancies
6) Post-migration: run two-week drift audit and create follow-ups for any edge-case uncovered
qa_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint CAS and duplicate/drop logic
Integration test harness that simulates clients producing ordered, out-of-order, and replayed fragments with randomized delays
Chaos test: kill aggregator instances mid-checkpoint to validate atomicity and idempotency
Load test: simulate sustained 10k sessions/s with small fragments to validate 99th percentile latency and PG/Redis contention
E2E billing validation: compare billed tokens from legacy pipeline vs new checkpointed pipeline on shadow traffic for 48h
